newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil aims for 90 mln tns grain production 97/98.
newsitem.headline: Brazil aims for 90 mln tns grain production 97/98.

text.p: The Brazilian government wants to beef up the country's infrastructure to cope with a 1997/98 grains harvest of 90 million tonnes, up from about 80 million tonnes in 1996/97, an official said.

Celio Floriani, special aide to Agriculture Minister Arlindo Porto, said the agriculture, finance and planning ministries were cooperating to ensure federal infrastructure investment helped reduce production costs for the agricultural sector.
"We can raise production to 90 million tonnes from 80 million tonnes really easily," he said. "But it's no good producing more if you don't have the infrastructure."
Floriani said the current port, road and warehousing system could cope with a maximum grains harvest of 80 million tonnes, which he said was the projection for 1996/97.
"Anything above that and we run into serious problems because of lack of infrastructure.
The last estimate by the ministry's Agricultural Supply Company (Conab) predicted a 1995/96 grains harvest of 74.2 million tonnes, down 8.5 percent on the previous crop.
Floriani said the ministries were joining forces to reduce the cost of doing business, the so-called "Brazil Cost".

They agreed to plough investment into ports and roads, the main components of the Brazil Cost. In addition, the government is pushing a tax reform package through Congress, which Floriani said would benefit agriculture.

The investment is part of a $54 billion infrastructure plan for the next two years which the government announced in August. Only $10 billion will come from government coffers and the rest from the private sector.
